title: Practice Note of the Board of Review: Linked Appeals Across Unemployment Insurance Appeals Dockets
content:
Appeals under **Unemployment Insurance Appeals** are linked across dockets and levels. A Board of Review appeal may be filed only against a lower-authority appeal that has been decided, and it names that appeal as its parent appeal; a dismissed lower-authority appeal reaches the Board only after its reopening was denied. Appeals of the same parties that arise from the same facts — a separation decision and the overpayment it created, or a benefit charge and the separation behind it — are heard together on one hearing date where the dockets allow consolidation, and the decision on the earlier issue governs the later one. When hearing slots are short, dockets are scheduled in the order of their scheduling priority.

## 1. Access to the Board of Review

A Board of Review appeal is authorized by the Department's records of the lower-authority appeal it names as parent, read before the Board appeal is accepted:

| The named lower-authority appeal | Board of Review appeal |
|---|---|
| has been decided | may be filed, naming that appeal as its parent |
| was dismissed, and its reopening was denied | reaches the Board |
| was dismissed, and its reopening has not been denied | does not reach the Board |
| has not been decided (still filed or scheduled) | may not be filed |

The Board appeal always names the one lower-authority appeal it seeks review of; an appeal that names no decided parent is not a Board of Review appeal.

## 2. Hearing related appeals together

Two conditions together place related appeals on one hearing date: the appeals are of the same parties and arise from the same facts, and the dockets concerned allow consolidation. Two such pairs are named:

- a separation decision and the overpayment it created;
- a benefit charge and the separation behind it.

When such appeals are heard together, the decision on the earlier issue — the separation, in both instances above — governs the later one.

## 3. Order of scheduling when slots are short

Each docket carries a scheduling priority rank, 1 first. When hearing slots are short, a docket with a lower rank number is scheduled before a docket with a higher one.

## Questions answered

- *A lower-authority appeal was dismissed. When can it reach the Board of Review?* Only after its reopening was denied; a dismissal on which reopening has not been denied does not reach the Board.
- *Which decision controls when the separation appeal and the resulting overpayment appeal are heard together?* The decision on the earlier issue, the separation, governs the overpayment appeal.
